slides.title: Executive summary

paragraphs.text: Executive summary
Parcelbird should not launch its own delivery service in 2027 and should put its cash into the software business instead
Quick commerce grows fast, but no operator has made it pay without raising prices
–	US quick-commerce sales nearly tripled in three years, to $5.1B in 2025
–	Both incumbents lose money per order; QuickBasket closed 4 of its 11 cities
Parcelbird Now would lose money per order; the plan works only on inputs no site has reached
–	At the benchmark median, an order loses $2.67 before store costs
–	The plan beats the best site on basket size, rider speed and density
Launching would break the board's runway rule, even on the founders' numbers
–	The plan leaves $2.5M at month 18, half of a year's runway at today's burn
–	At median economics each store would lose about $2.0M a year
Scaling the software reaches breakeven within current cash, if sales outgrow today's pipeline
–	The pipeline is worth up to $3.6M of ARR, for $0.8M a year of hires
–	At 60% growth the software breaks even in 2029, using about $6.62M
